solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Old soldier volunteers to guard object in long conflict (8)

indicatorNotes.to guard: VET TA stands round END, protecting it the way a guard would

blocks.note: TA = Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
an end = an aim or object

annotation.surface: An old soldier and some volunteers mount a guard over something during a long war.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Object' reads as a thing being guarded; it is an aim, as in 'to what end?'. The guard goes in after the first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a feud that runs on for years, often between families, is a long conflict.

entries.clue: Seaport winding ropes are made from this (7)

indicatorNotes.winding: the letters of SEAPORT are wound into a new order

annotation.surface: At a seaport, ropes are wound on the quay, and someone notes what they are made from.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a descriptive phrase rather than a synonym; 'winding' sits nicely with rope-making.
annotation.definitionFit: Esparto is a tough Spanish and North African grass used to make rope, paper and mats.

entries.clue: Opera put on originally in Avignon bombed (3,8)

indicatorNotes.originally: take the original, first letter of 'in'
indicatorNotes.bombed: Avignon plus that I is blown apart and rebuilt

annotation.surface: An opera is staged in Avignon and flops badly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a plain link word placing the opera in Avignon; it is fodder, giving its first letter. 'Bombed' works both as 'flopped' and as the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Don Giovanni is Mozart's opera about the seducer Don Juan.

entries.clue: Piece of chicken slightly tainted, under temperature (5)

indicatorNotes.under: in a down answer, HIGH is written below T

blocks.note: meat or game that is high has started to go off

annotation.surface: A piece of chicken that has been left out too long, just starting to smell.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue is a food-safety warning; 'under temperature' sounds like undercooking, but it only places HIGH beneath T.
annotation.definitionFit: The thigh is the upper leg joint of a chicken.

entries.clue: Ah, Fagin is out for foreign currency (7)

indicatorNotes.is out: the letters of AH FAGIN are put out of order

annotation.surface: Someone discovers Fagin, Dickens's thief-master, has gone off to change money abroad.
annotation.walkthrough: Fagin is the fence in Oliver Twist, so 'out for foreign currency' reads like a crook on the make.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Afghanistan's unit of money is foreign to a British solver.

entries.clue: Notice a mechanism emitting energy (6)

indicatorNotes.emitting: the device gives off, so loses, its E

annotation.surface: Someone spots a machine giving off energy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Notice' reads as a verb, 'spot'; it is the noun, as in an advice note telling you a delivery is coming.
annotation.definitionFit: Advice can mean a formal notice, as in a shipping advice or remittance advice.

entries.clue: Close attachment present in whirling dance (9)

indicatorNotes.in: HERE goes inside the spun dance
indicatorNotes.whirling: DANCE spins into a new order, ADNCE

blocks.note: present = here, as when answering a register

annotation.surface: Two dancers spin round clinging tightly to each other.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift; it is the roll-call reply. The surface pictures a couple locked together mid-spin.
annotation.definitionFit: Adherence is sticking fast to something, a close attachment.

entries.clue: Through exam, having avoided third (3)

indicatorNotes.having avoided third: VIVA leaves out its third letter

blocks.note: a viva is an oral exam
the third letter of VIVA, dropped

annotation.surface: A student gets through an exam but misses out on a third-class degree.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Third' sounds like a British degree class; it only means the third letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the preposition: travelling by way of a place is going through it.

entries.clue: Money handler hiding shillings in notebook (7)

indicatorNotes.hiding: to hide something is to keep it tucked away inside, so the notebook holds S within it

blocks.note: a cahier is a notebook, French-style
s = shillings, the old British coin

annotation.surface: A bank clerk keeps shillings tucked away in a notebook.
annotation.walkthrough: The notebook word is French, borrowed into English; the shilling was a pre-1971 British coin, still a crossword staple for S.
annotation.definitionFit: A cashier handles the money in a bank or shop.

entries.clue: Tattoos hearts amid fruits — these give a wavy edging (7,6)

indicatorNotes.amid: INKINGS and H go in the middle of PEARS

annotation.surface: A tattoo of hearts among fruit, with a wavy border round it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tattoos' sounds like a verb with 'hearts' as its object; both are nouns giving letters. The split in the fruit falls straight after its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Pinking shears are dressmaking scissors with notched blades that cut a zigzag edge to stop fraying.

entries.clue: Spirit of divine vengeance enveloping island (6)

indicatorNotes.enveloping: to envelop is to wrap up completely, so WRATH closes round I

annotation.surface: An avenging god's spirit engulfs an island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spirit of divine vengeance' reads as one phrase; the definition is only 'Spirit'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a ghost, especially the pale apparition of a person seen near death.

entries.clue: A uniform half-dozen balls returned one run or bye (2,6)

indicatorNotes.returned: OVER comes back the other way

blocks.note: in cricket an over is six balls from one bowler

annotation.surface: Cricket: a scorer tallies an over, a single, and a bye.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bye' pretends to be the cricket extra, fitting the run and the over; it is goodbye.
annotation.definitionFit: A borrowed French farewell, used in English as a slightly arch way of saying goodbye.

entries.clue: What shows inner workings of six over six division (11)

indicatorNotes.over: in a down answer, the first VI is written above the second

annotation.surface: A maths sum: six over six, a fraction to divide.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Six over six division' looks like arithmetic; it is VI above VI above SECTION.
annotation.definitionFit: Vivisection is cutting open a living animal, which exposes how its insides work.

entries.clue: What depends on current movement when India overwrites European court’s verdict? (10)

indicatorNotes.overwrites: I is written over E, replacing it

blocks.note: convection is heat carried by moving currents of fluid
I = India, NATO alphabet; goes in

annotation.surface: A physics question about currents turns into a ruling from a European court.
annotation.walkthrough: 'European court' reads as one unit; the E is wordplay and the definition starts at 'court’s'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in legal use: a finding of guilt is what a criminal court's verdict delivers.

entries.clue: What’s used to ring hill fort above a river (9)

indicatorNotes.above: in a down answer, CAMP sits on top of A NILE

blocks.note: ancient British hill forts are often called camps

annotation.surface: Something used to encircle a hill fort sitting above a river, like a ditch or wall.
annotation.walkthrough: 'To ring' suggests surrounding the fort; it is ringing bells, and a campanile houses them.
annotation.definitionFit: A campanile is a bell tower, the place from which bells are rung.

entries.clue: Change egg supplier when the first is off (4)

annotation.surface: Switch to a new egg supplier after the first batch went off.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a shopper changing egg supplier; the 'supplier' is an organ.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to alter something, or to become different, as prices and moods do.

entries.clue: Sailor’s back in working port in Scotland (4)

indicatorNotes.back: going back means going the wrong way, so AB is read right to left as BA
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' sets the sailor inside the word for working, so BA sits within ON

annotation.surface: A sailor is back at work in a Scottish harbour town.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sailor’s' is 'sailor is'; BA sits between O and N.
annotation.definitionFit: Oban is a ferry port on the west coast of Scotland.

entries.clue: Loaf of bread rose? (7)

blocks.note: a long crusty British loaf with diagonal slashes across the top
a rose is something that blooms

annotation.surface: Did the loaf rise in the oven?
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rose' reads as the past of rise, as dough does; it is the flower, and the question mark flags a whimsical sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a British bread loaf; a rose, a flower, is a thing that blooms.

entries.clue: Monsieur remains to fire fashionable people in society (10)

blocks.note: embers are what remains of a fire

annotation.surface: A Frenchman stays on to sack trendy people from a club.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Remains' reads as a verb and 'fire' as sacking; together they are a noun phrase, the remains belonging to a fire.
annotation.definitionFit: A collective noun: the whole body of people who belong to a club or society.

entries.clue: Assembly of certain vase broken by overturning support (7)

indicatorNotes.broken by: MING is split open to let TEE in
indicatorNotes.overturning: in a down answer TEE is turned upside down

blocks.note: a Ming is a particular kind of Chinese vase
a golf tee supports the ball

annotation.surface: A particular vase shatters when its stand tips over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Support' suggests the vase's stand; it is the small peg a golf ball sits on.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a gathering of people come together for a purpose.

entries.clue: I’m nearly sent electronic message to have an effect (7)

blocks.note: pinged = sent a quick electronic message, less its last letter

annotation.surface: Someone almost fires off an email in the hope of making a difference.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' sits right after 'I’m' in the surface but applies to 'sent electronic message'.
annotation.definitionFit: Usually followed by 'on': to make an impact on something, to affect it.

entries.clue: Admit one is drunk in control (8)

indicatorNotes.is drunk: ADMIT ONE staggers into a new order

annotation.surface: Confess that one is drunk while in charge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Admit one' looks like a ticket or a confession; it is just the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to have command over people or events.

entries.clue: Reserve power in bodybuilder’s exhausted muscle (6)

indicatorNotes.in: ICE and P go inside the emptied word
indicatorNotes.exhausted: bodybuilder's is emptied, leaving only B...S

blocks.note: to ice = to put on ice, hold in reserve

annotation.surface: A worn-out bodybuilder draws on reserve power in a muscle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Exhausted' means emptied here, not tired: bodybuilder's loses everything but its outer letters.
annotation.definitionFit: The biceps is the large muscle at the front of the upper arm.

entries.clue: Poet billions associated with Windermere? (5)

blocks.note: Windermere is England's largest lake; the ? marks an example

annotation.surface: A poet linked to Windermere, as the Lake poets were.
annotation.walkthrough: Windermere suggests Wordsworth and the Lake Poets; the answer is a different poet, William Blake.
annotation.definitionFit: William Blake was an English poet and artist.

entries.clue: I am quiet over story about a pharaoh’s fate? (13)

indicatorNotes.over: I'M MUM is turned over, giving MUMMI
indicatorNotes.about: 'about' in its sense of 'around': the story is placed around A

annotation.surface: Someone falls silent after telling a tale about the fate of a pharaoh.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A pharaoh’s fate' reads as one phrase, but the A belongs to the wordplay. The question mark marks the definition as an example: mummification befell pharaohs.
annotation.definitionFit: Egyptian pharaohs were mummified after death, so mummification was their fate.

entries.clue: Update government ministry (3)

blocks.note: short for modify, as gamers and car tuners use it
the UK's defence department, by its initials

annotation.surface: A news item about a government department issuing an update.
annotation.walkthrough: MoD is the UK's Ministry of Defence.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a clipped informal verb for altering something, and the initials of Britain's Ministry of Defence.

entries.clue: Cross groom initially interrupting his partner (6)

indicatorNotes.interrupting: to interrupt is to break in on something, so G breaks into the middle of BRIDE

blocks.note: a groom's partner is his bride

annotation.surface: An angry groom cuts across his new wife.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like the adjective 'angry'; it is the verb, to span.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb sense: to span a river or gap is to provide a way across it.

entries.clue: Man captures sea eagle around South Island (8)

indicatorNotes.captures: to capture is to take and hold, so the man holds the eagle-and-S inside him
indicatorNotes.around: 'around' in its sense of 'encircling': the eagle goes round S

blocks.note: the erne is the white-tailed sea eagle

annotation.surface: A man catches a sea eagle on an island in the south.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Man' tempts as the Isle of Man, an island itself, but it is only a fellow; the definition is at the other end.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: one of the Channel Islands, off the coast of Normandy.
